Their research focus, as evidenced by their published articles, spans several interdisciplinary areas including arts and creative practice, futures and philosophy, culture and identity, language and literacy, and climate and disaster. Within these areas, they show a particular frequency of work in arts and creative practice, which appears in four of their items, and futures and philosophy, which appears in three items.

Their work explores the intersection of various fields. For example, they have examined the intersection of biological mortality and advancing lifelike technologies in the context of death, degrowth, and finitude in the age of the lifelike. They have also explored the tension between climate change and the space race through somatic experiences, speculative design, and interactive performance. Their research includes the BUKAS Lab, which is a collaborative platform and physical space designed to foster pluridisciplinary initiatives at the intersection of art, design, technology, and futures literacy, specifically within the context of sustainable development and socioeconomic justice in the Global South.

Pieter Steyaert has also investigated the integration of art into transdisciplinary research practices, specifically looking at how collaborative art can facilitate idea generation and engagement within transdisciplinary sustainability research. Their work includes an artistic inquiry into space settlement ideology using rotifer experiments on board the ISS, which examines the tension between the human desire for cultural immortality and the biological necessity of adaptation in extreme environments. Additionally, they have worked on immersive installations, such as RE/ME, which is designed to reimagine and resculpt bodily self-perception through auditory and vibrotactile stimuli, acting as a cognitive aid and learning scaffold to help individuals develop self-sensing capabilities.

Because they have not advised any theses in this repository, there is no information available regarding their thesis supervision patterns, specific topics they have supervised, the years they have supervised, or how many students they have supervised. Their strengths in specific topics can only be inferred from their own articles, which demonstrate an interest in the intersections of art, technology, sustainability, and speculative futures. Their research involves themes such as ecology, cultural immortality, and the use of immersive installations to explore bodily perception. Based on the available data, they engage with complex questions involving biological engineering, artificial life, and the social implications of technological advancement.
